prompt.context_jp: 留守堂の声は穏やかだったが、その目___万智の顔から少しも離れなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 留守堂の声は穏やかだったが、その目___万智の顔から少しも離れなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that best fits: voice was calm, BUT the eyes (contrastively) didn't leave her face.

feedback.correct_en: は sets up a contrast with 声は穏やかだった — the voice was calm, but the eyes were a different story. This contrastive は is exactly what the だったが pivot needs.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would just introduce the eyes as new info without the contrastive pivot. を doesn't fit — 離れる is intransitive here.

contrast_examples.jp: 口は笑っているが、目は笑っていない。
contrast_examples.en: The mouth is smiling, but the eyes aren't.

prompt.context_jp: 黒板の隅には、誰か___消し忘れた白い線がかすかに残っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 黒板の隅には、誰か___消し忘れた白い線がかすかに残っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the relative clause subject.

feedback.correct_en: Inside a relative clause (誰か…消し忘れた) the subject takes が. 誰か is also new, unspecified info — a classic が trigger.
feedback.incorrect_en: は can't mark the subject inside a noun-modifying clause here. を would make 誰か the object, which breaks the sentence.

prompt.context_jp: 「あの時と同じ気持ちで 僕___今も あなたを愛しています｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「あの時と同じ気持ちで 僕___今も あなたを愛しています｡」
prompt.prompt_en: Rusudou's confession line — choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 僕 is the established topic (speaker's self-declaration), and this is a statement about himself: 僕は…愛しています. は establishes the thematic subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: 僕が would sound like 'it is I (and no one else) who loves you' — too exhaustive/identifying for a quiet confession. を already appears later for あなたを.

contrast_examples.jp: 僕はあなたを愛しています。
僕があなたを愛している。

prompt.context_jp: 「私___あなたを愛していません｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「私___あなたを愛していません｡」
prompt.prompt_en: Machi's reply. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: は is the natural topic marker in a self-declaration — 'As for me, I don't love you.' It parallels his 僕は in the previous turn.
feedback.incorrect_en: 私が would be exhaustive-listing ('I'm the one who doesn't love you'), oddly selective. 私も would mean 'me too (don't love you)', nonsensical here.

contrast_examples.en: I'll be the one to do it. (exhaustive)

prompt.context_jp: 万智の足音___廊下の向こうへ遠ざかり、教室には留守堂ひとりが残された。
prompt.prompt_jp: 万智の足音___廊下の向こうへ遠ざかり、教室には留守堂ひとりが残された。
prompt.prompt_en: Narrative description — choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: The footsteps are a newly introduced scene element observed in the moment — a classic descriptive が. The sentence paints what happens, it doesn't comment about an established topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 足音 a contrastive topic, which doesn't fit a pure scene description. を doesn't work with the intransitive 遠ざかる.

prompt.context_jp: 棚の間を所在なくうろついていると、聞き覚えのある甲高い声___背中に飛んできた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 棚の間を所在なくうろついていると、聞き覚えのある甲高い声___背中に飛んできた。
prompt.prompt_en: A voice suddenly calls out — choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: The voice is new, unexpected information bursting into the scene — perfect for が. Sudden sensory events (sounds, sights appearing) take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn 声 into an established topic, which clashes with the surprise 'suddenly from behind'. に would mean 'to the voice', breaking the sentence.

prompt.context_jp: どれほど遅く帰って来ても家事に手を抜かないの___、この妻の流儀だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: どれほど遅く帰って来ても家事に手を抜かないの___、この妻の流儀だった。
prompt.prompt_en: 'That [specific thing] was this wife's way.' Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: Here the nominalized clause 〜ないのが identifies/defines what her way is — exhaustive-listing が in an 'X is Y' identification. 'The thing that IS her style = never cutting corners.'
feedback.incorrect_en: のは would reverse the information structure, treating the clause as topic and 流儀 as new — awkward here. を doesn't fit the copular pattern.

contrast_examples.jp: 優しいのが彼の魅力だ。
contrast_examples.en: Being kind is his charm. (identifying が)

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の魅力は優しいところだ。
contrast_examples.en: His charm is his kindness. (topic は)

prompt.context_jp: 「こちらのリビング___ 東向きとなっております｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「こちらのリビング___ 東向きとなっております｡」
prompt.prompt_en: Machi describing the living room to clients.

feedback.correct_en: は presents the living room as the topic being described — standard pattern for 'as for X, X is Y' explanations in a sales pitch.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it exhaustive — 'THIS living room (not another) faces east', which doesn't match the neutral descriptive tone.

contrast_examples.jp: この部屋は南向きです。

contrast_examples.en: This room is the biggest. (exhaustive comparison)

prompt.context_jp: どちらの部屋も広さはほぼ同じで、窓からは柔らかな午後の光___入ってくる。
prompt.prompt_jp: どちらの部屋も広さはほぼ同じで、窓からは柔らかな午後の光___入ってくる。
prompt.prompt_en: Scene description — choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: The afternoon light is a newly described sensory element — perceptual が. Also, 窓からは already carries the は, so a second は would be awkward.
feedback.incorrect_en: 光は would stack another contrastive topic on top of 窓からは. を doesn't fit intransitive 入る here.

contrast_examples.en: Wind comes in through the window.

prompt.context_jp: 「私___不動産屋です｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「私___不動産屋です｡」
prompt.prompt_en: Machi's dry self-identification.

feedback.correct_en: Standard self-introduction/characterization: 私は〜です. She's defining her role, not identifying who among several is the realtor.
feedback.incorrect_en: 私が不動産屋です would mean 'I'm the realtor (not someone else)' — exhaustive, unnatural as a flat identity statement here.

prompt.context_jp: 「私に売れない家___ありません！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「私に売れない家___ありません！」
prompt.prompt_en: Machi's signature declaration.

feedback.correct_en: は emphasizes the nonexistence — 'as for houses I can't sell, there are none.' This contrastive-emphatic は is her trademark catchphrase.
feedback.incorrect_en: 家がありません would be a neutral 'there are no houses', losing the emphatic 'such a thing doesn't exist' punch she wants.

prompt.context_jp: 「僕は君に 三軒家さんに 愛情を抱いていると言ったけど 三軒家さんに 僕を愛してくれ と言ったこと___ない｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「…三軒家さんに 僕を愛してくれ と言ったこと___ない｡」
prompt.prompt_en: Rusudou carefully clarifies the limits of what he said.

feedback.correct_en: は contrasts this with the previous clause ('I told you I love her, BUT I've never told HER to love me'). Classic contrastive は with a 〜こと pattern of denial.
feedback.incorrect_en: ことがない would be a plain existential denial without the contrastive link to the preceding admission. を doesn't fit ない.

contrast_examples.en: I've never gone (contrary to what you might think).

prompt.prompt_en: Yashiro asks whether Machi was working alone.

feedback.correct_en: で marks the manner/state — '(working) by yourself'. 一人で is the standard adverbial 'alone'.
feedback.incorrect_en: 一人に would mean 'to one person' (direction/target). 一人を would make it a direct object.

prompt.context_jp: 「本日 ご紹介する物件は 今 お住まいの所から見て 東南___位置します｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「…東南___位置します｡」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'is located in the southeast'.

feedback.correct_en: 位置する ('to be located') takes に for the location of existence/placement — a fixed collocation.
feedback.incorrect_en: で marks the place of an action, not a location of being. を would make 東南 the object, which doesn't work with the intransitive 位置する.

contrast_examples.en: The station is located to the east.
I'll wait at the station. (action location)

prompt.context_jp: 「…外___の恋愛は自由にしようって 話し合ったんです｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「外___の恋愛は自由にしようって 話し合ったんです｡」
prompt.prompt_en: 'Love affairs OUTSIDE (our marriage)' — choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: で marks the location where the activity (恋愛) happens: 'love carried on OUTSIDE'. The ので pattern 外での〜 modifies the noun with a location-of-action phrase.
feedback.incorrect_en: 外にの is ungrammatical as a noun modifier for an activity location. 外をの doesn't form a valid phrase.

contrast_examples.en: A shop that is outside. (location of existence)

prompt.context_jp: 「お風邪の時は…｡ これが とっても よく___んですよ｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「これが とっても よく___んですよ｡」
prompt.prompt_en: The lady recommending ginger kudzu — 'this really ___ well.'

feedback.correct_en: 効く means 'to be effective' (of medicine/remedy) — the standard collocation 薬が効く / 風邪に効く.
feedback.incorrect_en: 聞く means 'to listen/hear'. 利く can mean 'to work/function' in some fixed phrases (気が利く) but is not the kanji used for medicine working.

prompt.context_jp: 問いただせば、自分の器の小ささをさらけ出すようで___。
prompt.prompt_jp: 問いただせば、自分の器の小ささをさらけ出すようで___。
prompt.prompt_en: 'If I pressed her on it, it would feel like exposing how petty I am, and I ___.'

feedback.correct_en: 気が引ける = 'to feel reluctant/hesitant, to shrink back from doing something.' Perfectly captures Yashiro's hesitation to question his wife.
feedback.incorrect_en: 気がつく = 'to notice'. 気にする = 'to worry about' — grammatically needs an object and doesn't fit the standalone clause-ending slot.

prompt.context_jp: 「風水が完璧な この家に お住まいになれば ご商売は さらに発展し 予算のオーバー分なぞ ___になるかと存じます｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「予算のオーバー分なぞ ___になるかと存じます｡」
prompt.prompt_en: Machi's grand sales pitch — 'the budget overrun will become ___.'

feedback.correct_en: 屁の河童 ('fart of a kappa') is a set idiom meaning 'nothing at all, a trivial matter'. Machi uses this colorful expression to downplay the price overrun.
feedback.incorrect_en: 猫の手 appears in 猫の手も借りたい ('so busy I'd borrow even a cat's paw'). 馬の耳 appears in 馬の耳に念仏 ('words wasted on the uninterested').

contrast_examples.en: I need all the help I can get.

prompt.context_jp: 庭野は___があったら入りたい気持ちで、ひたすらうつむいていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 庭野は___があったら入りたい気持ちで、ひたすらうつむいていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Niwano, deeply embarrassed, wished he could disappear.

feedback.correct_en: 穴があったら入りたい ('if there were a hole, I'd want to crawl into it') is the standard idiom for extreme embarrassment.
feedback.incorrect_en: 口 and 手 don't form this idiom. The image is specifically about a hole in the ground to hide in.

contrast_examples.jp: 恥ずかしくて穴があったら入りたい。
contrast_examples.en: I'm so embarrassed I want to disappear.

prompt.context_jp: 「それから こう ___を刺して来ます｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「こう ___を刺して来ます｡」
prompt.prompt_en: Niwano vows to warn Rusudou firmly.

feedback.correct_en: くぎを刺す ('to drive in a nail') = to give someone a firm warning, to put one's foot down. Standard idiom.
feedback.incorrect_en: 針を刺す or 刀を刺す aren't idiomatic in this 'warn someone sternly' sense.

contrast_examples.jp: 遅刻しないよう くぎを刺した。
contrast_examples.en: I warned him firmly not to be late.
I pricked my finger with a needle. (literal)

prompt.context_jp: 「人前で夫婦関係 ___ようになったら それは もう末期症状ですね～！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「人前で夫婦関係 ___ようになったら…」
prompt.prompt_en: Shirasu teasing Yashiro: 'When you start ___ your marriage in public, it's already a terminal symptom.'

feedback.correct_en: 取り繕う = 'to patch up appearances, to cover up for the sake of looks'. Fits defending a shaky marriage publicly.
feedback.incorrect_en: 取り消す = 'to cancel/retract'. 取り戻す = 'to recover/get back' — neither matches the 'put up a front' nuance.

contrast_examples.en: To cover up with a smile.

prompt.context_jp: 人気の美容院を二軒も___夫婦は、商売柄か、何かと縁起を担ぐたちらしかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 人気の美容院を二軒も___夫婦
prompt.prompt_en: 'The couple who ___ two popular beauty salons.'

feedback.correct_en: 切り盛りする = 'to manage/run (a business or household) skillfully'. The exact verb for running shops.
feedback.incorrect_en: 切り替える = 'to switch'. 切り裂く = 'to tear apart'. Neither means 'manage a business'.

prompt.context_jp: 庭野はグラスに目を落とし、留守堂の言葉を胸の中で何度も___。
prompt.prompt_jp: 留守堂の言葉を胸の中で何度も___。
prompt.prompt_en: 'Niwano turned Rusudou's words over and over in his heart.'

feedback.correct_en: 胸の中で言葉を転がす is a vivid collocation — 'rolling words around inside', mulling them over.
feedback.incorrect_en: 落とす ('drop') and 投げる ('throw') don't carry the sense of pondering/mulling.

contrast_examples.jp: 言葉を胸の中で転がす。
contrast_examples.en: To turn words over in one's heart.
To be at a loss for words.

prompt.context_jp: After being praised that she could become a feng shui master, Machi coolly deflects.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds most natural as Machi's deadpan reply?

choices.text: 私が不動産屋をしています。

feedback.correct_en: The crisp 私は不動産屋です matches Machi's clipped professional self-definition — simple topic-is-X.
feedback.incorrect_en: B overexplains with 〜をしています and uses が, sounding like identifying herself among others. C (私のは) is ungrammatical here.

prompt.context_jp: Yashiro reflects: coming home, no one is there.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing fits the lonely, resigned mood best?

choices.text: 家に帰っても、待っている人はいない。
家に帰っても、待っている人がいない。
家に帰っても、人は待っていない。

feedback.correct_en: 待っている人はいない emphasizes the pointed absence ('there's no one who waits') — natural for melancholy reflection.
feedback.incorrect_en: B with が is grammatical but flatter — more a plain observation. C reorders unnaturally and sounds like a general claim about 'people'.

contrast_examples.jp: 知っている人はいない。
contrast_examples.en: There's no one I know. (emphatic absence)

prompt.context_jp: Machi correcting a client's feng-shui misconception in sales mode.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds most natural for Machi's polite professional refusal?

choices.text: それはいけません。玄関正面の鏡は良い運をはじき返してしまいます。
それだめ。玄関の前の鏡は運をはじくよ。
それはいけませんよ。鏡がある玄関は運がはじきます。

feedback.correct_en: A matches Machi's crisp 丁寧 sales register: それはいけません + explanatory 〜してしまいます. Clean and authoritative.
feedback.incorrect_en: B drops into casual speech, unsuitable for a client. C has an awkward 鏡がある玄関は運がはじきます construction.

prompt.context_jp: Rusudou's reflective speech about silent affection.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version best captures Rusudou's thoughtful tone?

choices.text: ただ ひそかに思う それは不倫なんかじゃない。
ただ こっそり考える それは不倫じゃないよ。
ただ 密かに感じる それは浮気ではない。

feedback.correct_en: ひそかに思う ('to secretly hold [feelings]') is the natural collocation for silent romantic affection, and 〜なんかじゃない adds the dismissive emphasis fitting Rusudou's conviction.
feedback.incorrect_en: こっそり考える sounds like 'thinking stealthily' — more mischievous than romantic. 密かに感じる is unnatural; 感じる doesn't pair with 密かに for feelings-of-love.

contrast_examples.jp: ひそかに思いを寄せる。

prompt.context_jp: Shirasu answers Yashiro's question about why she's at the drugstore.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds most natural for Shirasu's blunt, casual tone?

choices.text: 見れば分かんでしょ バイトしてるんです。
ご覧になれば お分かりでしょう アルバイトをしております。
見たら 分からんですか バイトですよ。

feedback.correct_en: A mixes the casual 分かんでしょ with 〜んです — Shirasu's trademark blunt-but-still-addressing-boss register. Fits her character.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is too polite/stiff for Shirasu, who talks to Yashiro casually. C mixes dialectal 分からんですか awkwardly and loses her punchy rhythm.

contrast_examples.en: You can tell by looking, right? (casual-blunt)

contrast_examples.jp: ご覧になればお分かりでしょう。
contrast_examples.en: You would see upon looking. (stiff keigo)
